findings.title: deleteMany retryCount branch is not scoped to SMS reminders
findings.body: The new OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` in the `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany` call has no `method` (or `scheduled: false`) constraint, while the other branch is correctly scoped to `WorkflowMethods.SMS`. `retryCount` is a column on every WorkflowReminder row (EMAIL, SMS, WHATSAPP), so the SMS cron will permanently delete email/WhatsApp reminders as soon as anything else increments their retry counter, and it will also delete rows that have already been successfully scheduled (referenceId set) but happened to accumulate retries, losing the ability to later cancel the external job. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (and ideally `scheduled: false`) to that branch.

findings.title: retryCount updated with a read-modify-write instead of an atomic increment
findings.body: Both update calls set `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value read earlier in the request. If two cron invocations overlap (cron overrun, manual trigger, or a retrying scheduler), both read the same `retryCount` and write the same value, so failures are undercounted and the reminder can be retried indefinitely — exactly the loop this PR is trying to stop. Use Prisma's atomic `data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } }`.

findings.title: No retry counting when message or sendTo is missing, so those reminders still loop forever
findings.body: `retryCount` is only incremented inside the `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo)` block or in the catch. Reminders that have no `sendTo` (e.g. missing/blank attendee phone number) or an empty rendered message silently fall through every cron run with `scheduled: false` and `retryCount: 0`, and are re-processed on every invocation until `scheduledDate` passes. The same applies to the `continue` at line 68-70 when `workflowStep`/`booking` is null. The stated goal of the PR (stop endlessly reprocessing unschedulable reminders) is therefore only partially achieved.

findings.title: Prisma update inside catch can throw and abort processing of remaining reminders
findings.body: The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` added at the top of the catch block is not itself guarded. If that write fails (connection error, row deleted concurrently by the deleteMany above — P2025 record not found), the exception propagates out of the `for` loop and out of `handler`, so all remaining unscheduled reminders in this run are skipped and the endpoint returns a 500 instead of the `{ message: "SMS scheduled" }` response. Wrap the update in its own try/catch (or `.catch()`).

findings.title: OR-ed delete predicate on unindexed retryCount forces a full scan of WorkflowReminder
findings.body: The delete condition is now `(method = SMS AND scheduledDate <= now) OR retryCount > 1`. `retryCount` has no index and the OR prevents the existing `[method, scheduled, scheduledDate]` index from satisfying the whole predicate, so Postgres will likely sequentially scan the entire WorkflowReminder table on every cron run. On a large table this makes the cron noticeably slower and takes row locks broadly; consider issuing two separate scoped deletes or adding an index covering the retry condition.

findings.title: No tests for the new retry/delete behaviour
findings.body: The PR introduces new deletion semantics (drop reminders once retryCount > 1) and new increment paths (scheduleSMS returning falsy, and thrown errors), but no unit/integration test is added. Regressions such as deleting reminders of the wrong method or never incrementing the counter would not be caught; a test asserting retryCount increments on failure, that a reminder is removed after the second failure, and that non-SMS reminders are untouched would protect this logic.
